1	# SMA-830: let a tool declare a provider tool type
2	
3	Linear: [SMA-830](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-830/let-a-tool-declare-a-provider-tool-type-native-anthropic-memory).
4	Consumer: SMA-789 (the agent host's `memory` tool).
5	
6	## Intent
7	
8	The agent host (SMA-789) ships a custom `memory` tool. That tool copies the
9	commands, argument names and return strings of Anthropic's `memory_20250818`
10	tool, and it puts the protocol text in its description. Claude is trained on
11	the native tool, and the API adds the memory protocol to the system prompt only
12	when the request contains the native entry.
13	
14	This change lets a Helikon tool declare a provider tool type. The Anthropic
15	provider then sends the native entry:
16	
17	```json
18	{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}
19	```
20	
21	That entry has no `description` and no `input_schema`. All other providers
22	continue to send the generic schema. The host can change to the native type
23	with no change to its schema.
24	
25	## Goals
26	
27	- A `Tool` can declare zero or more provider tool types.
28	- Each declaration names a provider, a type string, and optional extra JSON
29	  fields. The extra fields cover tools such as `text_editor_20250728`
30	  (`max_characters`) and `computer_*` (display size). The limit: a tool has at
31	  most one type per provider, and the provider sends that type to every model.
32	  A tool type that depends on the model generation (for example the
33	  `text_editor` versions) needs the opt-out below.
34	- The Anthropic provider sends the typed entry when the tool declares an
35	  `anthropic` type. It sends the generic entry when the tool declares none.
36	- The OpenAI (Chat and Responses), Gemini, Bedrock and LiteLLM providers ignore
37	  the declaration and send the generic schema.
38	- Each provider has a test for both paths.
39	
40	## Non-goals
41	
42	- Native support on Bedrock. The Anthropic docs list the memory tool as
43	  supported on Amazon Bedrock, but our Bedrock provider uses the Converse API.
44	  A follow-up Linear issue covers it. LiteLLM can also route to Claude, but it
45	  uses the OpenAI wire format, so it also sends the generic schema.
46	- A `#[tool]` macro attribute for provider types. The SMA-789 host implements
47	  `Tool` by hand. A macro attribute can follow if a user asks for it.
48	- Server-side Anthropic tools (for example `web_search_*`). Those tools run on
49	  Anthropic's side and return no `tool_use` for Helikon to run. They need a
50	  different design.
51	- A model-dependent choice of type. The declaration is static.
52	  `AnthropicModelBuilder::native_tool_types(false)` is the opt-out for a model
53	  or gateway that does not know the type.
54	- Validation of the tool name against the type. For example, `memory_20250818`
55	  requires the name `memory`. The provider does not check this. The API
56	  returns a 400 error if the name is wrong.
57	
58	## Anti-goals
59	
60	- A change in behaviour for a tool that declares no provider type. The request
61	  bytes for such a tool must stay the same on every provider.
62	- A change in the serialized form of an existing `ToolDef`. Old serialized data
63	  must still deserialize, and a `ToolDef` with no provider types must serialize
64	  to the same JSON as today. The persisted carrier is the Temporal `call_model`
65	  activity input (`CallModelArgs.request: ModelRequest`,
66	  `runtime-temporal/src/activity_input.rs:262-268`), which goes into Temporal
67	  history. `AgentPlan` is not serialized.
68	
69	## Approaches
70	
71	Two decisions were open. Sven made both of them.
72	
73	**Shape of the declaration.**
74

# SMA-830: let a tool declare a provider tool type

Linear: [SMA-830](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-830/let-a-tool-declare-a-provider-tool-type-native-anthropic-memory).
Consumer: SMA-789 (the agent host's `memory` tool).

## Intent

The agent host (SMA-789) ships a custom `memory` tool. That tool copies the
commands, argument names and return strings of Anthropic's `memory_20250818`
tool, and it puts the protocol text in its description. Claude is trained on
the native tool, and the API adds the memory protocol to the system prompt only
when the request contains the native entry.

This change lets a Helikon tool declare a provider tool type. The Anthropic
provider then sends the native entry:

```json
{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}
```

That entry has no `description` and no `input_schema`. All other providers
continue to send the generic schema. The host can change to the native type
with no change to its schema.

## Goals

- A `Tool` can declare zero or more provider tool types.
- Each declaration names a provider, a type string, and optional extra JSON
  fields. The extra fields cover tools such as `text_editor_20250728`
  (`max_characters`) and `computer_*` (display size). The limit: a tool has at
  most one type per provider, and the provider sends that type to every model.
  A tool type that depends on the model generation (for example the
  `text_editor` versions) needs the opt-out below.
- The Anthropic provider sends the typed entry when the tool declares an
  `anthropic` type. It sends the generic entry when the tool declares none.
- The OpenAI (Chat and Responses), Gemini, Bedrock and LiteLLM providers ignore
  the declaration and send the generic schema.
- Each provider has a test for both paths.

## Non-goals

- Native support on Bedrock. The Anthropic docs list the memory tool as
  supported on Amazon Bedrock, but our Bedrock provider uses the Converse API.
  A follow-up Linear issue covers it. LiteLLM can also route to Claude, but it
  uses the OpenAI wire format, so it also sends the generic schema.
- A `#[tool]` macro attribute for provider types. The SMA-789 host implements
  `Tool` by hand. A macro attribute can follow if a user asks for it.
- Server-side Anthropic tools (for example `web_search_*`). Those tools run on
  Anthropic's side and return no `tool_use` for Helikon to run. They need a
  different design.
- A model-dependent choice of type. The declaration is static.
  `AnthropicModelBuilder::native_tool_types(false)` is the opt-out for a model
  or gateway that does not know the type.
- Validation of the tool name against the type. For example, `memory_20250818`
  requires the name `memory`. The provider does not check this. The API
  returns a 400 error if the name is wrong.

## Anti-goals

- A change in behaviour for a tool that declares no provider type. The request
  bytes for such a tool must stay the same on every provider.
- A change in the serialized form of an existing `ToolDef`. Old serialized data
  must still deserialize, and a `ToolDef` with no provider types must serialize
  to the same JSON as today. The persisted carrier is the Temporal `call_model`
  activity input (`CallModelArgs.request: ModelRequest`,
  `runtime-temporal/src/activity_input.rs:262-268`), which goes into Temporal
  history. `AgentPlan` is not serialized.

## Approaches

Two decisions were open. Sven made both of them.

**Shape of the declaration.**

- A. A type string only. This is small, but it cannot express
  `text_editor` or `computer` parameters.
- **B. A type string plus optional extra JSON fields (chosen).** This covers
  every Anthropic client tool for a small increase in surface.
- C. A closed enum per known tool. This gives strong types, but each new tool
  version needs an SDK release.

**Carrier from `Tool` to the provider.**

- **1. A new field on `ToolDef`, and `ToolDef` becomes `#[non_exhaustive]`
  (chosen).** The declaration stays with the tool definition, and later fields
  are no longer breaking. Cost: a breaking change to `paigasus-helikon-core`
  and a release of all dependents.
- 2. A side map on `ModelRequest`, keyed by tool name. This is not breaking,
  but the data is not on the tool definition. Each provider must look it up by
  name, and code that builds a `ToolDef` by hand can forget the map.

**Rejected: a provider-side mapping**, for example
`AnthropicModelBuilder::native_tool("memory", ProviderToolType)`. It needs no
core change and no breaking release. But the declaration is then separate
from the tool, and a name-based mapping applies to every agent on that model.
The ticket asks for the tool to declare the type.

## Design

### Core (`paigasus-helikon-core`, `src/model.rs` and `src/tool.rs`)

A new public type:

```rust
/// A provider-defined tool type that a tool declares, for example
/// Anthropic's `memory_20250818`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct ProviderToolType {
    /// The provider id, for example `"anthropic"`.
    pub provider: String,
    /// The provider's type string, for example `"memory_20250818"`.
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    pub type_name: String,
    /// Extra fields that the provider puts into its tool entry.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "serde_json::Map::is_empty")]
    pub params: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
}

Each provider uses only the first entry with its own id. The `///` comment
says: declare at most one entry per provider.

```rust
impl ProviderToolType {
    pub fn new(provider: impl Into<String>, type_name: impl Into<String>) -> Self;
    pub fn with_params(self, params: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>) -> Self;
}
```

A new method on `Tool`, with a default:

```rust
/// Provider tool types that this tool declares. Default: none.
/// A tool that wraps another tool (a decorator) must forward this method.
/// If it does not, the declaration is lost.
fn provider_types(&self) -> &[ProviderToolType] { &[] }
```

- It gets `pub provider_types: Vec<ProviderToolType>`, with
  `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`.
- It becomes `#[non_exhaustive]` and derives `PartialEq`. The precedent for
  this pattern is `ModelCapabilities` (`model.rs:267-299`).
- It gets constructors:

  It copies `provider_types` from the tool.

core (`src/agent.rs`, `src/loop_state.rs`, `tests/wire_serde.rs`), anthropic
(9 in 6 files), bedrock (19 in 3 files), gemini (7 in 4 files), litellm (2),
openai `tests/live.rs` (2), runtime-temporal `src/worker.rs` (1), and
`tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs` (6). The CLI has no
`ToolDef` literal. No code destructures `ToolDef`. The synthetic handoff
`ToolDef` in `loop_state.rs` has no provider types.

The facade needs no source change: `pub use paigasus_helikon_core as core;`
and core's `pub use model::*` already expose
`paigasus_helikon::core::ProviderToolType`. Do not add a second re-export.

### Anthropic provider (`src/translate/tools.rs`)

For each `ToolDef`:

1. Find the first entry in `provider_types` with `provider == "anthropic"`.
2. If there is one, and the builder did not set `native_tool_types(false)`,
   the tool entry is its `params` without a `cache_control` key. Then
   `"type"` is set to `type_name` and `"name"` is set to the `ToolDef` name.
   `type` and `name` are set last, so a `type` or `name` key in `params` cannot

   `params` contains those keys (they pass through, as documented). The
   `cache_control` key is removed because `translate/cache.rs` owns cache
   breakpoints, and an extra breakpoint can exceed the limit of four. A
   `tracing::debug!` on target `paigasus::anthropic::translate` records each
   typed entry.
3. If there is none, the entry is the generic entry, as today.

The crate exports `pub const PROVIDER_ID: &str = "anthropic";` and documents

`PROVIDER_ID`, so the two cannot drift. A provider-agnostic tool crate can
write the literal `"anthropic"` instead of a dependency on this crate. A typo
such as `"Anthropic"` gives the generic entry with no error; the debug trace
helps to find it.

`AnthropicModelBuilder::native_tool_types(bool)` (default `true`) is the
opt-out. With `false`, every tool gets the generic entry. Use it for a model or
an Anthropic-compatible gateway that does not know a declared type.

The existing cache marker (`translate/cache.rs`) puts `cache_control` on the
last tool entry. The tool reference lists `cache_control` as an optional
property of Anthropic-provided tools, so no change is necessary.

The memory tool docs (fetched 2026-11-20) mark the tool `stable` and say: "the
memory tool itself doesn't require a beta header". The env-gated live test
below confirms this against the real API, with a typed entry plus
`cache_control`. If the API needs a header, the builder's existing `.beta(...)`
(`src/builder.rs:116`) is the documented way to send it.

### Runtime-temporal

`call_model` activity inputs carry `ModelRequest`, so `provider_types` goes
into Temporal history. A pre-0.8 activity worker in a rolling deploy reads the
new JSON (no `deny_unknown_fields`) but drops `provider_types`, so that turn
sends the generic entry. This is safe, but silent. The CHANGELOG notes it.

### Other providers

The OpenAI (Chat and Responses backends), Gemini, Bedrock and LiteLLM
translators do not read `provider_types`. Each gets one test: a `ToolDef` with
an `anthropic` provider type gives the same output as the same `ToolDef` with
no provider types.

### Tests

- Core: `ProviderToolType` serde round trip; an old `ToolDef` JSON without

  with no `provider_types` key (extend `tests/wire_serde.rs`);

  change, and every library dependent exposes core types. release-plz gives a
  dependent with no own commit only a patch. So:
  1. The PR title is `feat(core)!: SMA-830 ...`. The repo squash-merges with
     the PR title as the commit title, so the `!` must be in the title.
  2. The PR adds an upgrade note under `## [Unreleased]` in the CHANGELOG of
     core, the facade, and each library dependent of core. The CLI is exempt
     (binary crate, internal library). Then the `!` commit touches each of
     those crate directories, and release-plz gives each a minor bump.
  3. No version changes in this PR. No hand bump. (Release-ascend caveats 1
     and 2 apply only to a PR that bumps its own version.)
  4. Before the PR opens, squash the branch in a scratch clone and run
     release-plz **v0.4.3** `release-plz update`. Record the version table in
     the PR body. Every library dependent must show a minor bump (0.x) and
     core must show 0.8.0.

  hand. SMA-830 must merge only after SMA-838 PR 1 has published, so that the
  version base is the republished one. Rebase on `main` before step 4.

  cargo-semver-checks by default; the break is expected and the minor bump
  matches it.

+## Provider tool types
+
+Some providers define their own tool types. The Anthropic memory tool is one example. The provider expects a typed entry, not a name, a description and a schema. A tool declares such a type with `Tool::provider_types`.
+
+```rust,ignore
+use paigasus_helikon::core::ProviderToolType;
+use paigasus_helikon_providers_anthropic::PROVIDER_ID;
+
+fn provider_types(&self) -> &[ProviderToolType] {
+    &self.types // for example one entry: ProviderToolType::new(PROVIDER_ID, "memory_20250818")
+}
+```
+
+`ProviderToolType::new(provider, type_name)` names the provider and the type. Call `with_params` to add extra fields for the typed entry.
+
+A tool can declare at most one entry for each provider. The default is an empty slice, so an existing tool does not change.
+
+A tool wrapper must forward `provider_types` from the tool that it wraps. If the wrapper does not forward it, the typed entry is lost and the provider gets the generic schema.
+
+Anthropic is the only provider that uses this declaration now. It sends `{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}` for the memory tool. OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock and LiteLLM send the generic schema. See [Model Providers](./model-providers.md).

+## Provider tool types
+
+Some providers define their own tool types. The Anthropic memory tool is one example. The provider expects a typed entry, not a name, a description and a schema. A tool declares such a type with `Tool::provider_types`.
+
+```rust,ignore
+use paigasus_helikon::core::ProviderToolType;
+use paigasus_helikon_providers_anthropic::PROVIDER_ID;
+
+fn provider_types(&self) -> &[ProviderToolType] {
+    &self.types // for example one entry: ProviderToolType::new(PROVIDER_ID, "memory_20250818")
+}
+```
+
+`ProviderToolType::new(provider, type_name)` names the provider and the type. Call `with_params` to add extra fields for the typed entry.
+
+A tool can declare at most one entry for each provider. The default is an empty slice, so an existing tool does not change.
+
+A tool wrapper must forward `provider_types` from the tool that it wraps. If the wrapper does not forward it, the typed entry is lost and the provider gets the generic schema.
+
+Anthropic is the only provider that uses this declaration now. It sends `{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}` for the memory tool. OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock and LiteLLM send the generic schema. See [Model Providers](./model-providers.md).

## SMA-830 whole-branch review (56442a0b..48db057e)

I did the review in one pass. I read the full source diff, the spec and the ledger. I spawned no subagents and made no change to HEAD, the index or the working tree.

**Checks that I ran:**
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean.
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p paigasus-helikon-core -p paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic --no-deps` is clean.
- `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic --lib translate`: 83 passed.
- markdownlint on the changed `.md` files: 0 issues.
- `git merge-tree HEAD main`: 4 conflicts. Details are under Recommendations.

### Strengths
- **No change for a tool that declares no provider type.**
  - The only production change outside core and Anthropic is `runtime-temporal/src/worker.rs:399`, which now calls `ToolDef::from_tool`.
  - The OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock and LiteLLM translators have no production diff, so they cannot read `provider_types`.
  - The generic Anthropic entry uses the same `json!` literal as before (`translate/tools.rs:39-43`).
- **The serialized form does not change.**
  - `provider_types` has `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]` (`core/src/model.rs:132`).
  - Tests prove that the old JSON decodes and that a plain `ToolDef` serializes to the old JSON (`tests/wire_serde.rs:86-102`).
  - There is a frozen Temporal literal for the old shape and the new shape (`activity_input.rs:793-819`).
  - Temporal rule 3 is satisfied: when an old worker drops the field, it sends the generic entry. This is safe, and the field does not touch authorization.
- **The seams are correct.**
  - `ToolDef::from_tool` replaces both former mapping sites (`agent.rs:909`, `worker.rs:399`). `register()` keeps `provider_types`, and a test proves it (`worker.rs:818`).
  - The synthetic handoff def has no types (`loop_state.rs:748`).
  - The structured-output tool is added after `translate_tools`, so it takes the cache marker and the typed entry stays the same. A test covers this (`translate/mod.rs:429`).
  - The cache marker on a typed last entry is tested (`translate/mod.rs:415`).
  - `type` and `name` are set last, and `params` cannot override them. `cache_control` is removed from `params`.
- **The public API is complete.** A downstream crate can still make every `ToolDef` that it made before: `ToolDef::new` plus the public fields, which it can still read and assign. `ProviderToolType::new` and `with_params` set every field. Every new public item has a `///` comment. No public item links to a private item.
- **The CHANGELOG notes are complete.** All 19 crates get a note (core, the facade and 17 library dependents). The CLI is exempt. `macros` depends on core only as a path-only dev-dependency, so it correctly gets no note. The notes agree with the code.
- **Main adds no new `ToolDef {` literal.** The one literal on main (`anthropic/tests/live.rs:212`) is the same literal that this branch already changed.

### Issues

#### Critical
None.

#### Important
1. **The live Anthropic test has not run.**
   - Location: `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/live.rs:300-326` (`memory_typed_tool_smoke`).
   - Problem: Only this test proves two claims against the real API: that the memory tool needs no beta header, and that the API accepts a typed entry with `cache_control`. The wiremock test (`tests/messages_wire.rs:223`) only shows that the code sends no beta header. It cannot show that the API accepts the request.
   - Effect: `native_tool_types` defaults to `true`. If the API needs a header, every request from SMA-789 that has the memory tool fails with a 400 error.
   - Fix: Run `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic --test live memory_typed_tool_smoke -- --ignored` with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set, before the merge. Record the result in the PR body. The ledger already plans to show this at Gate 2. I keep it here because it is the only check of a default-on behaviour against the real API.

#### Minor
1. **No test covers the public opt-out setter.**
   - Location: `builder.rs:140` and `builder.rs:214`.
   - Problem: `builder_opt_out_reaches_body` (`translate/mod.rs:457`) sets `cfg.native_tool_types = false` directly. If `build_config` stops copying the field, every test still passes.
   - Fix: Add one test that calls `AnthropicModelBuilder::new(..).native_tool_types(false).build_config()` and asserts on the body.
2. **Two documented behaviours are not in the public docs.**
   - Problem: Keys such as `description` and `input_schema` in `params` pass through to the typed entry, and `cache_control` is removed. The spec says that this behaviour is "as documented". But the only text is on the `pub(crate)` `translate_tools`, and it says "No description or schema is sent".
   - Fix: Add one sentence to the `ProviderToolType::params` doc (`core/src/model.rs:188`) or to the Anthropic README. No test covers the pass-through.
3. **Book issues in `docs/book/src/concepts/tools.md`.**
   - Line 126 imports `paigasus_helikon_providers_anthropic::PROVIDER_ID`, but line 125 uses the facade path. For facade users the import is `paigasus_helikon::anthropic::PROVIDER_ID`.
   - Line 122 says that the provider expects a typed entry "not a name, a description and a schema". The typed entry has a name.
4. **`Tool::provider_types` returns `&[ProviderToolType]`, and the type holds `String` fields.** Because of this, a static declaration needs a `OnceLock` (see the test at `worker.rs:777-786`) or a struct field. This is not a defect. A later change could use `Cow<'static, str>` if users complain.
5. **`ToolDef::from_tool` needs a turbofish when a tool implements `Tool<Ctx>` for every `Ctx`**, for example `ToolDef::from_tool::<(), _>(&Plain)` (`tool.rs:492`). This is not a defect.
6. **Deferred Minors in the ledger.**
   - The redundant `Null` assert in `tests/wire_serde.rs:117-120` is harmless. Leave it.
   - The ledger does not describe the 2 style Minors from Task 3. In my review of the diff, none of them blocks the merge.
   - None of the ledger's deferred items must be fixed before the merge.
7. **A code fence in the spec is not closed.** The `rust` fence that opens at spec line 106 is not closed before the prose at line 120. This is a display problem only, because the spec is excluded from lint.

### Recommendations (Task 6 / process)
- **Rebase on `main` before you squash and run release-plz.** `main` has 3 new commits (#368, #369, #370). `git merge-tree` shows 4 conflicts:
  - `providers-anthropic/CHANGELOG.md`
  - `providers-anthropic/tests/live.rs` (keep both new tests: `memory_typed_tool_smoke` and `nested_tool_use_inside_open_round_is_accepted`)
  - `runtime-agentcore/CHANGELOG.md`
  - `crates/paigasus-helikon/CHANGELOG.md`

  All 4 are mechanical: keep both sides. The other files merge with no conflict.
- **Obey the HOLD in the ledger (SMA-838).** Do not merge, and do not suggest a merge of release PR #371, until SMA-838 PR 1 has merged and published. Tell `paigasus-helikon-87` before any merge.
- **Release steps.** The PR title needs `feat(core)!:`. Record the release-plz v0.4.3 version table in the PR body: core 0.8.0 and a minor bump for every dependent. Confirm in CI that the macros trybuild failure (3/12) also occurs on `main`. The ledger shows this item as open.

### Declined to judge
- How release-plz treats the hand-written "Upgrade notes" under `## [Unreleased]`, and whether the cascade gives each crate a minor bump. Reason: Task 6 and SMA-838 own the release mechanics.
- Temporal replay: on replay, activity inputs now differ from history for a tool that declares a type. Reason: I think that the SDK does not compare activity input payloads on replay, but I did not check this in the SDK source. A changed tool description has the same effect today.
- Native types on Bedrock, validation of the tool name against the type, and server-side tools. Reason: the spec lists these as non-goals.
- Ordering inside the typed entry. Reason: the workspace does not enable `serde_json/preserve_order`, so keys serialize in sorted order, and the order has no meaning on the wire.

### Assessment
**Ready to merge: With fixes.** The fix is Important 1: run the live test once. Also do the planned rebase and keep the SMA-838 hold. The Minor items are optional.

**Reasoning:** The code agrees with the spec. A tool with no provider type gets the same request bytes and the same serialized form as at the baseline, on all providers. The breaking core change is intended, and the `ToolDef` and `ProviderToolType` constructors let a downstream crate make every definition it made before. Only the default-on Anthropic typed entry is not yet checked against the real API.
